$comment: #FEED-237 (Danny: 'like whatsapp'): a person's OWN message in a session or chat ×4 (web `components/agent-session.tsx` + `hooks/use-session-outbox.ts`, desktop `ui::steer_viewer` + `ui::session_chat` + `domain::message_delivery`, iOS ExpCore `MessageDelivery.swift` + `AgentSessionView`, Android `domain/MessageDelivery.kt` + `AgentSessionScreen`) is ONE bubble at the bottom of the transcript from the moment Send is pressed; NOTHING about it sits above the composer (dock.json has no `queued` card any more). SEND: the session composer (a `sessionId`: a live or idle session, a chat, an agent's conversation) clears its field AND its synced draft (composer-draft.json) at the press and puts an OUTBOX entry {clientId (a fresh UUID, also the `sessions.send` `clientMessageId`), text (trimmed), createdAt (the press), state `sending`, messageId null} at the bottom; the send (uploads, then `sessions.send`) runs on a scope that outlives the screen. The server took it = the entry's messageId = the result's; it failed = state `failed` (no toast: the bubble says so). The outbox is PERSISTED per session on the device (web localStorage `exp-outbox:<sessionId>`, desktop the data dir's `outbox.json`, iOS the GRDB `outbox` table, Android the `outbox` Room table) so a reload or an app restart keeps every entry; on start a `sending` entry with no messageId is SENT AGAIN with the same clientMessageId (F21: the server returns the row it already stored, never a second one), a `failed` one waits for its Retry. A composer without a session (the launch composer that STARTS a chat, a comment) keeps composer-send.json. STATE = deliveryState(input) (`stateCases`): input {local: the outbox entry's state (`sending` | `failed`) or null (no entry: a synced row alone), stored: the server holds the row (an entry's messageId set, or a synced row), deliveredAt / consumedAt: the synced row's (null without one), echoed: the bubble IS the live transcript's echo of the turn (the device replayed it into the agent's conversation)}; first match wins: echoed or consumedAt = `read` (TWO checks: processed into the session), deliveredAt = `sent` (ONE check: the device received it and holds it in its queue while a turn runs), local `failed` and not stored = `failed`, anything else = `sending` (the CLOCK: not stored yet, or stored while the session's device has not received it: offline, a slow link, a device that has not picked it up). DELIVERED: `messages.delivered_at` (synced) is stamped by the DEVICE the moment its pickup receives a pending row, before the turn takes it (`sessions.delivered {sessionId, messageIds}`, idempotent, only rows still NULL; `sessions.consume` stamps it too when it is still NULL, `sessions.claim` with the first message); a server without the column reads as never delivered (`sending` until consumed). DEDUPE (`outboxCases`, outboxMerge(input) → {drop: clientIds, keep: clientIds}): an entry is superseded, and DROPS from the outbox (its synced row's bubble takes its place, same position), once a synced row carries its messageId; an entry still without a messageId (a send in flight, a reload before the answer) matches the OLDEST unmatched own row (authorKind user, authorId = the viewer) whose body equals its text and whose createdAt is no earlier than the entry's createdAt minus `matchWindowMs`, each row matching at most one entry, entries oldest first; a `failed` entry never matches (the server has nothing). Everything else is kept, in createdAt order (ties by clientId). ORDER: the transcript's rows (with NO feed yet: steer-enet.json SENT INPUTS, the consumed person inputs, drawn as these same own bubbles reading `read`, above the placeholder's copy), then the viewer's own synced rows the device has not consumed (oldest first), then the kept outbox entries; a consumed row is the transcript's echo from then on (that bubble reads `read`). HANDOFF (no flicker, `handoffCases`, ownHandoff(input) → the ids of the consumed own rows that still draw): a bubble NEVER vanishes between its row being consumed and the transcript row that echoes it appearing; until then the consumed row keeps its own bubble (reading `read`) in the own tail, after the transcript and before the not-consumed rows, oldest first (createdAt, then id). Input {viewerId, now, feedEmpty (the transcript has no feed: SENT INPUTS draws the consumed inputs, so nothing is held), rows (the session's synced rows), echoes (the transcript's person rows of the main lane, in transcript order: {text, at (ms, null when the feed carries none)})}. Candidates: the viewer's own card-less rows (authorKind user, authorId = the viewer) with consumedAt set and consumedAt ≥ now − `handoffMaxMs` (a device that never echoes cannot hold a bubble forever), oldest first; each takes the FIRST echo not taken yet whose trimmed text equals its trimmed body (#FEED-239: OR, the session's first prompt, a BRIEFED echo = one that opens with `briefRequestHeading` (session-brief.json composes it: the Request section, then the brief's other sections, its image lines localized): the body with its attachment lines (`![…](/api/attachments/…)` / `[…](/api/attachments/…)`) removed and trimmed is non-empty and the echo after the heading starts with it) and whose at is null or ≥ its createdAt − `matchWindowMs`; a candidate with an echo is the transcript's (its bubble goes, the echo draws it: one bubble per message id, never two), one without is kept. The views re-evaluate when the rows or the transcript change and once `handoffMaxMs` after the newest kept row's consumedAt. A local desktop's session (elocal) follows the same rules: its device stamps `delivered_at` the moment its hub hears the row and `consumed_at` when the run takes it in (the launch's brief, a send into the live run), so its bubbles read one check, then two, like a cloud session's; a row that arrives while no run is live (the process exited, the app restarted, before the claim's run) starts or resumes the run with it as the prompt (local-parity.json WAKE), so it reaches two checks too. FILES: an entry's picked files are part of the entry: a device that persists the outbox persists them too (Android: the bytes under the app's files dir + the entry's `pending` names; desktop: the paths and the landed ids in `outbox.json`), uploads them before `sessions.send`, keeps every landed id on the entry as it lands, and on start resumes a `sending` entry's remaining uploads then sends it; a file that is gone (deleted, unreadable) fails the entry (Retry tries again, Delete drops it). A send with files is an outbox entry like any other ×4 (no older path). MARK: beside the bubble's `HH:mm`, inside the bubble at its bottom right, the time first: genUI `MessageStatus` (the catalogue's MessageBubble `status`), `marks[state]` = the icon concept and the tone (muted = the time's ink, info = the read blue, danger = destructive), 14 px, its accessibility label `copy.status[state]`. The `HH:mm` = the row's createdAt, an outbox entry's own until its row arrives. Every OTHER sender's bubble has no mark. ACTIONS (`actionCases`, bubbleActions({state, stored}) → ids in order, `copy.menu` labels): the bubble's menu (a pointer: right-click or the hover `…`; touch: long-press; the shared context menu / DropdownMenu, nothing new) offers `retry` + `delete` on a `failed` bubble (retry = send again with the SAME clientId, state back to `sending`; delete = drop the entry, its text gone), `cancel` on a stored `sending` or `sent` one (`sessions.unqueue`: the row is deleted and the device drops what it holds; once consumed the server refuses with CONFLICT and a toast reads `Couldn't remove the message`), nothing on an unstored `sending` one or a `read` one; a `failed` bubble's mark is itself a press target opening that menu. testIds: the mark `testIds.status` with `data-state` = the state, the menu `testIds.menu`.
